hints: Calculate the 8th term $u_8 = 50(0.8)^7$ and the 9th term $u_9 = 50(0.8)^8$.
Compare each term to $10\text{ mm}$ and state the conclusion clearly.
walkthrough:
Determine the common ratio $r$ of the geometric progression:
$$r = \frac{u_2}{u_1} = \frac{40}{50} = 0.8$$

Calculate the distances for the 8th and 9th impacts using $u_n = ar^{n-1}$ with $a = 50\text{ mm}$:
$$u_8 = 50(0.8)^7 \approx 10.486\text{ mm}$$
$$u_9 = 50(0.8)^8 \approx 8.389\text{ mm}$$

Conclude why the 9th impact is the first to sink less than $10\text{ mm}$:
Since $u_8 = 10.5\text{ mm} > 10\text{ mm}$ and $u_9 = 8.39\text{ mm} < 10\text{ mm}$, the 9th impact is confirmed as the first impact that sinks less than $10\text{ mm}$ into the ground.

ai_rubric.Geometric Progressions: Finds $r = 0.8$ (B1). Evaluates $u_8 \approx 10.5\text{ mm}$ and $u_9 \approx 8.39\text{ mm}$ (M1). Concludes explicitly that the 9th impact is the first below $10\text{ mm}$ (A1).

hints: Use the geometric series sum formula $S_n = \frac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}$ with $a = 50, r = 0.8, n = 20$.
Round the result to the nearest millimetre.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total depth to the nearest integer millimetre:
$$S_{20} \approx 247.12\text{ mm} \approx 247\text{ mm}$$

ai_rubric.Geometric Progressions: Applies sum formula with $n=20, a=50, r=0.8$ (M1). Evaluates to $247\text{ mm}$ to nearest integer (A1).

skill_tags: Sum to Infinity of a Geometric Progression

hints: Calculate the sum to infinity $S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r}$ using $a = 50$ and $r = 0.8$.
walkthrough:
Use the sum to infinity formula $S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - r}$ to find the greatest theoretical depth achievable:
$$S_\infty = \frac{50}{1 - 0.8} = \frac{50}{0.2} = 250\text{ mm}$$
